text:
The Canucks are 3-15-1 after Saturday's 4-2 loss in Edmonton, their fifth straight, and our simulations give them no realistic route to the playoffs. Seven points in 19 games is a season already pointed at the draft lottery.

The play is bad: 40 percent of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances), and 44 percent during the skid. The goaltending has made it worse. Vancouver's goalies have allowed about 15 more goals than the chances against them predict. Kevin Lankinen is .802 and 9.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, Leevi Meriläinen .848 and 6.2 worse. Our race model says the Canucks deserved about 6.5 more points than they have, which is cold comfort when the deserved number is still last-place hockey.

There are small things to hold on to. Elias Pettersson, the center, is "rediscovering his game in healthier environment," per Sportsnet, and the sell-high debate has started. Liam Ohgren has five points in ten, and Pass it to Bulis' Daniel Wagner gave the Canucks full credit for holding their own against the Oilers on Saturday. Filip Hronek reached 300 career points with the assist on Brock Boeser's goal. Hronek's pairing with the other Elias Pettersson, the young defenseman, has been outscored 11-5. That's the development project worth watching in a lost year.
headline: Vancouver is in free fall, and the goalies are part of it
